title: Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security
licence: Commonwealth of Australia, CC BY 4.0 (legislation.gov.au). Text condensed; consult the registered instrument.

companion_guidance: Prudential Practice Guide CPG 234 Information Security
summary: CPS 234 aims to ensure that an APRA-regulated entity takes measures to be resilient against information security incidents (including cyber-attacks) by maintaining an information security capability commensurate with vulnerabilities and threats. The Board is ultimately responsible. Key mandates include asset classification by criticality/sensitivity, control design and systematic testing by independent specialists, internal audit assurance (including third-party assurance), and strict APRA notification timeframes (within 72 hours for material incidents, and within 10 business days for material control weaknesses).

clauses.heading: Objectives and key requirements of this Prudential Standard
clauses.text: This Prudential Standard aims to ensure that an APRA-regulated entity takes measures to be resilient against information security incidents (including cyber-attacks) by maintaining an information security capability commensurate with information security vulnerabilities and threats. A key objective is to minimise the likelihood and impact of information security incidents on the confidentiality, integrity or availability of information assets, including information assets managed by related parties or third parties. The Board of an APRA-regulated entity is ultimately responsible for ensuring that the entity maintains its information security.
subclauses: Clearly define the information security-related roles and responsibilities of the Board, senior management, governing bodies and individuals;
Maintain an information security capability commensurate with the size and extent of threats to its information assets, and which enables the continued sound operation of the entity;

Implement controls to protect its information assets commensurate with the criticality and sensitivity of those information assets, and undertake systematic testing and assurance regarding the effectiveness of those controls; and
Notify APRA of material information security incidents.
clauses.notes: Introductory summary framing the standard's statutory intent.

clauses.heading: Authority
clauses.text: This Prudential Standard is made under subsection 11AF(1) of the Banking Act 1959, subsection 32(1) of the Insurance Act 1973, subsection 230A(1) of the Life Insurance Act 1995, subsection 92(1) of the Private Health Insurance (Prudential Supervision) Act 2015, and subsection 34C(1) of the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993.
clauses.notes: Covers ADIs, General Insurers, Life companies, Private Health Insurers, and RSE licensees.

clauses.heading: Scope of Application
clauses.text: This Prudential Standard applies to all APRA-regulated entities defined as: (a) authorised deposit-taking institutions (ADIs), including foreign ADIs, and non-operating holding companies authorised under the Banking Act (authorised banking NOHCs); (b) general insurers, including Category C insurers, non-operating holding companies authorised under the Insurance Act (authorised insurance NOHCs), and parent entities of Level 2 insurance groups; (c) life companies, including friendly societies, eligible foreign life insurance companies (EFLICs) and non-operating holding companies registered under the Life Insurance Act (registered life NOHCs); (d) private health insurers registered under the PHIPS Act; and (e) RSE licensees under the SIS Act in respect of their business operations.
subclauses: ADIs and authorised banking NOHCs
General insurers, Category C insurers, insurance NOHCs, Level 2 groups
Life companies, friendly societies, EFLICs, registered life NOHCs
Private health insurers
RSE licensees under the SIS Act
clauses.notes: Applies across all prudentially regulated Australian financial institutions.

clauses.heading: Foreign Branches
clauses.text: The obligations imposed by this Prudential Standard on, or in relation to, a foreign ADI, a Category C insurer or an EFLIC apply only in relation to the Australian branch operations of that entity.
clauses.notes: Restricts foreign entity compliance obligations to their Australian branch footprint.

clauses.heading: Group Compliance
clauses.text: Where an APRA-regulated entity is the Head of a group, it must comply with a requirement of this Prudential Standard: (a) in its capacity as an APRA-regulated entity; (b) by ensuring that the requirement is applied appropriately throughout the group, including in relation to entities that are not APRA-regulated; and (c) on a group basis. In applying the requirements on a group basis, references in paragraphs 13 to 36 to an 'APRA-regulated entity' are to be read as 'Head of a group' and references to 'entity' are to be read as 'group'.
clauses.notes: Extends information security obligations to non-regulated subsidiaries within the financial group.

clauses.heading: Commencement
clauses.text: This Prudential Standard commences on 1 July 2019, subject to paragraph 6.
clauses.notes: In effect since 1 July 2019.

clauses.heading: Third Party Transition
clauses.text: Where an APRA-regulated entity's information assets are managed by a third party, the requirements in this Prudential Standard will apply in relation to those information assets from the earlier of the next renewal date of the contract with the third party or 1 July 2020.
clauses.notes: Transitional period ended on 1 July 2020; all third-party arrangements are now fully subject to CPS 234.

clauses.heading: APRA Discretion to Adjust or Exclude
clauses.text: APRA may adjust or exclude a specific prudential requirement in this Prudential Standard in relation to an APRA-regulated entity.
clauses.notes: APRA discretion must be exercised in writing.

clauses.heading: Definitions
clauses.text: The following definitions are used in this Prudential Standard: availability refers to accessibility and usability when required; confidentiality refers to access being restricted only to those authorised; criticality refers to the potential impact of a loss of availability; information asset means information and information technology, including software, hardware and data (both soft and hard copy); information security means the preservation of an information asset's confidentiality, integrity and availability; information security capability means the totality of resources, skills and controls which provide the ability and capacity to maintain information security; information security control means a prevention, detection or response measure to reduce the likelihood or impact of an information security incident; information security incident means an actual or potential compromise of information security; information security policy framework means the totality of policies, standards, guidelines and procedures pertaining to information security; information security threat is a circumstance or event that has the potential to exploit an information security vulnerability; information security vulnerability is a weakness in an information asset or information security control that could be exploited to compromise information security; integrity refers to completeness, accuracy and freedom from unauthorised change or usage; sensitivity means the potential impact of a loss of confidentiality or integrity.
subclauses: availability: accessibility and usability when required
confidentiality: access being restricted only to those authorised
criticality: potential impact of a loss of availability
information asset: information and IT, including software, hardware and data
information security: preservation of confidentiality, integrity and availability
information security capability: totality of resources, skills and controls
information security control: prevention, detection or response measure
information security incident: actual or potential compromise of information security
information security policy framework: totality of policies, standards, guidelines, procedures
information security threat: circumstance/event with potential to exploit vulnerability
information security vulnerability: weakness that could be exploited
integrity: completeness, accuracy, freedom from unauthorised change/usage
sensitivity: potential impact of a loss of confidentiality or integrity
clauses.notes: Statutory definitions for all key cyber/info-security terms in CPS 234.

clauses.heading: Board Ultimate Responsibility
clauses.text: The Board of an APRA-regulated entity (Board) is ultimately responsible for the information security of the entity. The Board must ensure that the entity maintains information security in a manner commensurate with the size and extent of threats to its information assets, and which enables the continued sound operation of the entity.
clauses.notes: Footnote 4: For an RSE licensee, Board means Board of directors or group of individual trustees. Footnote 5: For a foreign ADI, Board refers to senior officer outside Australia.

clauses.heading: Definition of Roles and Responsibilities
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must clearly define the information security-related roles and responsibilities of the Board, senior management, governing bodies and individuals with responsibility for decision-making, approval, oversight, operations and other information security functions.
clauses.notes: Footnote 6: Governing bodies and individuals includes committees, working groups and forums.

clauses.heading: Commensurate Information Security Capability
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain an information security capability commensurate with the size and extent of threats to its information assets, and which enables the continued sound operation of the entity.
clauses.notes: Capability must scale with the institution's digital footprint and threat environment.

clauses.heading: Third Party and Related Party Capability Assessment
clauses.text: Where information assets are managed by a related party or third party, the APRA-regulated entity must assess the information security capability of that party, commensurate with the potential consequences of an information security incident affecting those assets.
clauses.notes: Footnote 7: Applies to all information assets managed by related/third parties, not only outsourced material activities.

clauses.heading: Active Maintenance of Capability
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must actively maintain its information security capability with respect to changes in vulnerabilities and threats, including those resulting from changes to information assets or its business environment.
clauses.notes: Requires dynamic updating as threat vectors evolve.

clauses.heading: Policy Framework Alignment
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain an information security policy framework commensurate with its exposures to vulnerabilities and threats.
clauses.notes: Must encompass all organizational security policies and guidelines.

clauses.heading: Direction on Responsibilities
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity's information security policy framework must provide direction on the responsibilities of all parties who have an obligation to maintain information security.
clauses.notes: Footnote 8: Parties includes staff, contractors, consultants, related parties, third parties, and customers.

clauses.heading: Asset Identification and Classification
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must classify its information assets, including those managed by related parties and third parties, by criticality and sensitivity. This classification must reflect the degree to which an information security incident affecting an information asset has the potential to affect, financially or non-financially, the entity or the interests of depositors, policyholders, beneficiaries or other customers.
clauses.notes: Criticality = impact of loss of availability; Sensitivity = impact of loss of confidentiality or integrity.

clauses.heading: Implementation of Information Security Controls
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must have information security controls to protect its information assets, including those managed by related parties and third parties, that are implemented in a timely manner and that are commensurate with: (a) vulnerabilities and threats to the information assets; (b) the criticality and sensitivity of the information assets; (c) the stage at which the information assets are within their life-cycle; and (d) the potential consequences of an information security incident.
subclauses: vulnerabilities and threats to the information assets;
the criticality and sensitivity of the information assets;
the stage at which the information assets are within their life-cycle (planning, design through decommissioning/disposal); and
the potential consequences of an information security incident.
clauses.notes: Footnote 9: Life-cycle refers to planning and design through to decommissioning and disposal.

clauses.heading: Evaluation of Third Party Control Design
clauses.text: Where an APRA-regulated entity's information assets are managed by a related party or third party, the APRA-regulated entity must evaluate the design of that party's information security controls that protects the information assets of the APRA-regulated entity.
clauses.notes: Footnote 10: Applies to all third-party managed information assets.

clauses.heading: Detection and Response Mechanisms
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must have robust mechanisms in place to detect and respond to information security incidents in a timely manner.
clauses.notes: Requires SOC / SIEM / monitoring capabilities to detect compromises quickly.

clauses.heading: Information Security Response Plans
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain plans to respond to information security incidents that the entity considers could plausibly occur (information security response plans).
clauses.notes: Response plans must cover plausible cyber breach and data loss scenarios.

clauses.heading: Content of Response Plans & Escalation
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity's information security response plans must include the mechanisms in place for: (a) managing all relevant stages of an incident, from detection to post-incident review; and (b) escalation and reporting of information security incidents to the Board, other governing bodies and individuals responsible for information security incident management and oversight, as appropriate.
subclauses: managing all relevant stages of an incident, from detection to post-incident review;
escalation and reporting of information security incidents to the Board, other governing bodies and individuals responsible.
clauses.notes: Full end-to-end incident lifecycle coverage.

clauses.heading: Annual Review & Testing of Response Plans
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must annually review and test its information security response plans to ensure they remain effective and fit-for-purpose.
clauses.notes: Mandates at least annual cyber tabletop or simulation testing.

clauses.heading: Systematic Control Testing Program
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must test the effectiveness of its information security controls through a systematic testing program. The nature and frequency of the systematic testing must be commensurate with: (a) the rate at which the vulnerabilities and threats change; (b) the criticality and sensitivity of the information asset; (c) the consequences of an information security incident; (d) the risks associated with exposure to environments where the APRA-regulated entity is unable to enforce its information security policies; and (e) the materiality and frequency of change to information assets.
subclauses: the rate at which vulnerabilities and threats change;
the criticality and sensitivity of the information asset;
the consequences of an information security incident;
risks associated with untrusted environments;
materiality and frequency of change to information assets.
clauses.notes: Footnote 11: Untrusted environments where the entity cannot enforce its policies.

clauses.heading: Assessment of Third Party Testing
clauses.text: Where an APRA-regulated entity's information assets are managed by a related party or a third party, and the APRA-regulated entity is reliant on that party's information security control testing, the APRA-regulated entity must assess whether the nature and frequency of testing of controls in respect of those information assets is commensurate with paragraphs 27(a) to 27(e) of this Prudential Standard.
clauses.notes: Footnote 12: Entity must verify that vendor testing aligns with CPS 234 standards.

clauses.heading: Escalation of Control Deficiencies
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must escalate and report to the Board or senior management any testing results that identify information security control deficiencies that cannot be remediated in a timely manner.
clauses.notes: Direct bridge to APRA notification in paragraph 36.

clauses.heading: Independent Testing Specialists
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must ensure that testing is conducted by appropriately skilled and functionally independent specialists.
clauses.notes: Testers (penetration testers, red teams, auditors) must be functionally independent from system operators.

clauses.heading: Annual Review of Testing Program
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must review the sufficiency of the testing program at least annually or when there is a material change to information assets or the business environment.
clauses.notes: Triggers on calendar basis (annual) or material changes.

clauses.heading: Internal Audit Scope & Control Assurance
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity's internal audit activities must include a review of the design and operating effectiveness of information security controls, including those maintained by related parties and third parties (information security control assurance).
clauses.notes: Internal audit must cover third-party and related-party environments.

clauses.heading: Internal Audit Skills
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must ensure that the information security control assurance is provided by personnel appropriately skilled in providing such assurance.
clauses.notes: Requires technical cyber audit competence.

clauses.heading: Internal Audit Assessment of Third Party Assurance
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity's internal audit function must assess the information security control assurance provided by a related party or third party where: (a) an information security incident affecting the information assets has the potential to materially affect, financially or non-financially, the entity or the interests of depositors, policyholders, beneficiaries or other customers; and (b) internal audit intends to rely on the information security control assurance provided by the related party or third party.
subclauses: incident has potential to materially affect entity or customer interests; and
internal audit intends to rely on third-party control assurance.
clauses.notes: Footnote 13: Applies to all third-party managed information assets.

clauses.heading: Mandatory 72-Hour Incident Notification to APRA
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must notify APRA as soon as possible and, in any case, no later than 72 hours, after becoming aware of an information security incident that: (a) materially affected, or had the potential to materially affect, financially or non-financially, the entity or the interests of depositors, policyholders, beneficiaries or other customers; or (b) has been notified to other regulators, either in Australia or other jurisdictions.
subclauses: (a) materially affected, or had the potential to materially affect, financially or non-financially, the entity or the interests of depositors, policyholders, beneficiaries or other customers; or
(b) has been notified to other regulators, either in Australia (e.g. OAIC under Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, ASD/ACSC, ASIC) or other jurisdictions.
clauses.notes: Footnote 14: Other regulators include domestic government agencies (OAIC, ASIC) and international regulators. Overlap with CPS 230: An incident reported under CPS 234 does not need to be separately reported under CPS 230.

clauses.heading: Mandatory 10-Business-Day Control Weakness Notification to APRA
clauses.text: An APRA-regulated entity must notify APRA as soon as possible and, in any case, no later than 10 business days, after it becomes aware of a material information security control weakness which the entity expects it will not be able to remediate in a timely manner.
clauses.notes: Triggers when a material control weakness cannot be remediated promptly.
